title: Music at the Roof Garden, Chris Kelly, and leaving Piron
summary: Roof Garden crowds wanted sweet Lombardo-style music not blues; Chris Kelly played jazz; Russ left Piron in 1930 for lower pay and the Depression.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Before we get to what he did, what kind of numbers did they like at the root garden and the rich white people?

Well, they played, they played, they played the modern music, now. He only had a band on the counter on the style of the lombardo. You see. And the people that go into the root garden was the type of people. It wasn't, you know, the people that wanted all these junk, you know. Blues and all that stuff. They wanted, you know, like the old people.
Well, no, Chris, not a Capcom. No. No. No.
If they moved to for dancing? Huh? If they moved to for dancing?
That's what I thought, it was a dance hall. Yeah. It was a dance hall.
Did people play some of his own numbers today?

Yeah. Mm-hm. He made a similar artistic cadence and all that kind of stuff. Well, Chris Keller, he used to play, in fact I played with Chris also at the Bo's, the Bo's Club. Well, Chris Keller did a jazz band, just like the Lola Band, the cream band, mostly a jazz band. And he wasn't a particular reading band, but he was a good jazz band.
But they would play Barrow House and all, Chris Keller? Oh yeah, he was a Barrow House man.
Put you in the air, that's what happened to his hobby.

That was his hobby. That was Chris Keller's hobby. Yeah. And uh. So it was an entirely different kind of music from Peele. Oh yeah, he was a fan that got Lombardi Band. Drick the music. And then you left Peele to go home. Well, after Peele got bad, we spent a little recording, and we went to the Peele, and we went to the Peele. So he phoned out to meet and things. I'd come on to, one night, depression, I'd sit in and say, Jesus, a butler rat. He told me a butler rat, he called him Gae. He saw it, one got killed. And I'd go to the Lavina, and put on the rats. Me, the butler rat, spook young, boot young, the boy that killed guy, uh, Walter Decker. I played there about two years. He brought me there. Well, depression set me. I said he's making thirty dollars a week. Remember what year that was? I had like thirty, thirty-two. Thirty or thirty-two. I left Peele in thirty. And I left Peele in thirty. And I go, I threw the Peele in the house. I had to leave the band, and I wasn't making enough money. But, me, it was all right. I left the band, and he got Alfred Williams to play in the band. But he changed his band around completely. At the time Peele went on the boat. He got rid of all the older fellas. But, Peele, I think Peele had died. And they got most of the young, the whole new young band, see? And I played after, you know, he'd taken about two years. A man started cutting out on the siren. I don't know if he did this guy in there, and he had a little deal in the iron and the other. But, I left the little deal. I quit the little deal. It goes on to the old Ashen house. With Biggie and Eddie Jones, this guy a couple years ago. And Willie Foster, my cousin. Myself.
